subject: convoyHauler
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: armoured convoy hauler guarding a sealed cargo pod.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a single TypeScript module for a vehicle, deciding it can be a static model since props don't strictly need joints. I'm sketching the design as a six-wheeled armored hauler with a front cab and a sealed cylindrical cargo pod on a long flatbed.

Now I'm working through dimensions and layout -- axle positions, wheel size, chassis height, and cab placement -- using box and cylinder helpers to build the frame and wheels, with a sloped windshield shaped via an extruded profile.

For the windshield I'm placing a small textured plane with cyan HUD lines angled along the slope normal, offset slightly outward from the cab surface. Then I'm working out the cargo pod as a capsule-like cylinder lying along the z-axis, sized and positioned to rest on top of the bed.

For the pod's finish, I'm skipping pre-built kits and writing my own paint logic: panel seams spaced along the length, separate glow-cyan ring bands at intervals, and hazard stripes using the SDK's paint and stripe utilities.

Now I'm placing cargo clamps—box cradles at the bed and thick dark-metal strap rings (torus geometry) wrapped over the pod at several z positions, mostly sinking slightly below the bed surface since a full ring would otherwise clip through. I'm also nailing down the pod's placement, centering its 5.6-unit-long cylindrical body around z=-1.4 with the front end facing the cab.

For the pod body itself, I'm using a 4.4-length cylinder with tapered frustum caps at each end (0.6 units long, 12-sided, radius shrinking from 1.15 to 0.7), rotated 90° on X so the cylinder's axis runs along z instead of y. I'm checking that the pod radius and center height clear the bed's width and height, and confirming the cab height sits comfortably below the pod's top.

Now I'm figuring out placement for the chassis, bed deck, and fenders over the wheels, working out the box dimensions and y-centers so each piece stacks correctly without clipping the wheels or pod.

Checking cab-wheel clearance confirms no overlap, so I'll keep the cab at 2.4 width. Now I'm adding cab details: a bull bar, glowing headlight boxes near the front, a dark grille, and an armored wedge-shaped front bumper.

Planning the side windows, roof turret with cylindrical base and gun barrels, a magenta light bar, antenna with glowing tips, and twin exhaust stacks positioned behind the cab.

Still designing wheels and details...

Now I'm thinking about armor plating on the pod, a rear sealing hatch with a hazard emblem texture, and decal placements for "CARGO // SEALED" text with a biohazard-style icon on the faceted pod sides, working out the geometry for flat plane placement against the cylinder's facets.

Rethinking the approach, I'm leaning toward a chamfered box shape instead of a faceted cylinder for the pod -- a low-poly cyberpunk container with an octagon-ish cross-section extruded along its length for a cleaner surface to apply decals to.

I'm giving the pod a gunmetal base with panel-line seams darkened periodically along z, warm-cool top-bottom lighting, and grime accents near the bottom. For accents, I'm adding thin octagonal strap rings near the ends plus small glowing cyan strip boxes running along the top of the pod.

I'm writing a helper function that generates the octagon outline points for the straps, then settling on a palette of dark navy hull, slate armor plates, magenta and cyan accents, and yellow hazard stripes, along with texture ideas like hazard stripe patterns, cargo labels, and hub details.

For the hull paint function, I'm blending a base gradient between darker and lighter navy depending on surface normal, layering in noise-based grime and wear patches, and darkening the lower portion to suggest dirt accumulation near the ground.

I'm setting up imports for noise, mixing, striping, and a glow effect from the kit, then planning a hazard bumper using yellow-and-dark diagonal stripes along the x-axis. I'm starting to write a builder helper function for creating boxes with position and color options.

Still placing axles and bed geometry...

Adding mirrors on arms, side decal planes with "CARGO" and hazard labeling, a number plate on the cab, and a rear pod door with a lock texture plus a stepped octagon rear cap.

I'm also placing a front cap and gooseneck connector box, and deciding to skip hose details in favor of simple cylinder rods instead of sweeps.

Now adding sensors: twin thin cylindrical antennas on the cab roof with glowing tips, plus a satellite dish made from a flipped cone geometry mounted on the pod. I'm also adding magenta underglow boxes beneath the chassis, checking that they clear the ground, and verifying the lowest point of the vehicle is where the tires touch y=0 given their radius and segment geometry.

I'm settling on a tire radius that keeps clearance correct, then moving to write the full component code efficiently, using rotated cylinders for side elements and mirrored arrays for symmetric parts, applying the glow helper to flat-colored pieces, and finishing with the metadata export.
